translations.simulation.cta.title: Put your project under strain
translations.simulation.cta.body: Before you commit your time and your money, find out under what conditions your business can work and what could make it fail.
translations.simulation.entry.title: Two ways to start
translations.simulation.entry.project.title: From an IDEM project
translations.simulation.entry.project.body: Business plan, market analysis, financial forecasts and business model are already there. The engine has less to ask for, and you pay less.
translations.simulation.entry.import.title: By importing your business plan
translations.simulation.entry.import.body: PDF, DOCX or plain text. IDEM extracts the activity, market, target customer, prices and costs, then lets you fill in the gaps before you start.
translations.simulation.offers.title: What you are buying
translations.simulation.offers.body: Simulation is billed separately from the rest of IDEM: it spends external research, several agents and compute. The amount is shown and confirmed before anything starts.
translations.simulation.offers.run.name: Simulation
translations.simulation.offers.run.body: The scenarios, the deciding factors, the major risks and the viability index.
translations.simulation.offers.pack.name: Simulation + report
translations.simulation.offers.pack.body: The simulation and its full report, cheaper than buying both separately.
translations.simulation.offers.report.name: Full report
translations.simulation.offers.report.body: The detailed analysis and recommendations, for a simulation you already ran.
translations.simulation.evidence.title: Every figure says where it came from
translations.simulation.evidence.body: Observed data, a derived estimate and an assumption are not worth the same. Blurring them would give a false impression of precision.
translations.simulation.evidence.data.label: Data
translations.simulation.evidence.data.body: An observed, published figure with its source and its date. Fuel prices, urban density, exchange rates.
translations.simulation.evidence.estimate.label: Estimate
translations.simulation.evidence.estimate.body: A value derived from comparable data, when nothing direct exists for your market.
translations.simulation.evidence.assumption.label: Assumption
translations.simulation.evidence.assumption.body: A deliberate choice by the engine, flagged as such, because no reliable data was available.
translations.simulation.wall.title: A business does not run on five variables
translations.simulation.wall.body: It runs on dozens, sometimes hundreds of factors, and they are never quite the same from one project to the next.
translations.simulation.wall.badge.label: factors typically identified on a single project, before a single scenario is run.
translations.simulation.wall.more: and many more, depending on your sector
translations.simulation.hero.title: Test your business before you {$START_TAG_SPAN}launch{$CLOSE_TAG_SPAN} it
translations.simulation.hero.description: An idea can look excellent on paper and still fail once it meets the market. IDEM looks for the factors that can genuinely influence your business, simulates several possible futures, and shows you where your model breaks.
translations.simulation.fan.title: Fan of simulated trajectories
translations.simulation.fan.desc: From a single project, the engine lets many trajectories diverge. A minority stay above the viability threshold; most fall below it.
translations.simulation.honesty.title: What IDEM Simulator does not promise you
translations.simulation.honesty.p1: The results are estimates based on the data, assumptions and scenarios available at the time of analysis.
translations.simulation.honesty.p2: A high index guarantees neither viability, nor profitability, nor the long-term survival of your business. A low index does not mean the project is impossible: it means that, in the scenarios that were run, some factors carry significant risk.
translations.simulation.honesty.p3: It is a decision-support tool. Not a prediction, not a guarantee.
translations.simulation.loop.title: A simulation is not an endpoint
translations.simulation.loop.body: Change your price, your target customer or your funding in IDEM, run it again, and compare the two versions. What moves is not your chance of succeeding: it is how much strain your model takes.
translations.simulation.loop.caption: Each new run is kept, so you can compare versions instead of arguing about them.
translations.simulation.how.title: What IDEM does when you start a simulation
translations.simulation.how.body: This is not a conversation with an AI. It is a five-stage analysis.
translations.simulation.how.card.body: Several agents work in parallel: one reads the project, others research external data, another combines them into scenarios.
translations.simulation.pipeline.read.title: Reading the project
translations.simulation.pipeline.read.body: IDEM builds a structured picture of your project, separating what it knows from what it has to research, what stays uncertain, and what is missing.
translations.simulation.pipeline.discover.title: Factor discovery
translations.simulation.pipeline.discover.body: Agents look for the factors that can actually move this particular business, then rank them as critical, important, secondary or uncertain.
translations.simulation.pipeline.research.title: Data research
translations.simulation.pipeline.research.body: Prices, density, costs, regulation, seasonality: every external value arrives with its source, its date and how much confidence it carries.
translations.simulation.pipeline.simulate.title: Simulation
translations.simulation.pipeline.simulate.body: The engine combines factors and runs baseline, favourable and adverse scenarios, stress tests, and rare compound shocks.
translations.simulation.pipeline.analyse.title: Analysis
translations.simulation.pipeline.analyse.body: Viability index, robustness, confidence level, breaking points, the conditions viability depends on, and recommendations ranked by priority.
translations.simulation.readout.title: An index, never on its own
translations.simulation.readout.body: An index of 72 backed by solid data and an index of 72 riddled with uncertainty do not mean the same thing. IDEM always shows both together.
translations.simulation.readout.robustness.def: How well the model keeps holding as the factors deteriorate.
translations.simulation.readout.confidence.def: The quality of the data the analysis rests on, assumptions included.
translations.simulation.readout.uncertainties.def: What the simulation could not establish, and what still has to be checked on the ground.
translations.simulation.readout.card.label: Simulated viability index
translations.simulation.readout.card.caveat: This index measures how robust the project is across the scenarios that were run. It is not a prediction of success.
translations.simulation.report.title: The report answers one question
translations.simulation.report.body: What could make this project succeed or fail, and what should I change?
translations.simulation.report.note: Not "improve your marketing". Rather: acquisition cost is the model's main weakness, test an organic channel before raising the ad budget. Expected impact high, priority critical, confidence medium.
translations.simulation.report.image.alt: A simulation report opened in IDEM, showing the financial summary and its indicators
translations.simulation.report.caption: The report is delivered inside your project, next to the deliverables it was built from.
translations.simulation.report.s4: Scenarios, stress tests and extreme cases
translations.simulation.report.s10: What to validate in the real world
translations.simulation.sectors.title: Factors depend on the business, not on a template
translations.simulation.sectors.body: Two businesses, two worlds. A fixed list of twenty variables applied to everyone would describe neither of them properly.
translations.simulation.sectors.delivery.name: Urban delivery
translations.simulation.sectors.farming.name: Farming
translations.simulation.sectors.farming.note: Western Cameroon, short supply chain, B2B
translations.simulation.stress.title: The point is not to reassure you. It is to find where the model breaks.
translations.simulation.stress.body: IDEM deliberately puts your business through hard situations, then tells you which ones it cannot take.
translations.simulation.stress.verdict.label: Verdict: no-go
translations.simulation.stress.verdict.body: When the conditions are genuinely bad, the engine says so, and lists exactly which scenarios the model could not survive.
translations.simulation.stress.q1: What happens if your main competitor cuts prices by 30%?
translations.simulation.stress.q2: What happens if your acquisition cost rises by 40%?
translations.simulation.stress.q3: What happens if you grow half as fast as planned?
translations.simulation.stress.q4: What happens if your funding lands six months late?
translations.simulation.stress.q5: What happens if a new regulation comes into force?
translations.simTerms.subtitle: Terms of Use for IDEM Simulation — business viability simulation
translations.simTerms.nav.project_creation: 7. THE PROJECT CREATED FROM YOUR PLAN
translations.simTerms.scope.title: 1. WHAT THESE TERMS COVER
translations.simTerms.scope.content: These terms apply to IDEM Simulation, the part of IDEM that puts a business project under stress and returns a viability index, scenarios, factors and a report. They come in addition to the IDEM Terms of Service and to the Privacy Policy, which continue to apply. Where a point is specific to simulation, this document prevails. You are asked to accept these terms before each run, because each run reads your project and sends an extract of it to artificial intelligence models.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.title: 2. WHAT A SIMULATION IS
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.content: A run proceeds in six stages: reading your project or your business plan, discovering the factors that could move it, gathering the external figures it can, building a numeric model, running scenarios on that model, and analysing what came out. The arithmetic is deterministic — the same figures always produce the same projection. What surrounds it is not: the choice of factors, the design of the scenarios and every written commentary are produced by AI models, which can be wrong.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.baseline: The whole model rests on around ten figures — price, variable cost, fixed costs, acquisition cost, growth, retention, starting capital. Where your project does not state one, the engine estimates it and says so.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.states: Every element is presented with its status: read in your source, to be researched, estimated, or missing. That distinction is part of the result and must not be dropped when the result is passed on.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.confidence: Every run carries a confidence level. A high viability index resting on assumptions is not the same claim as the same index resting on established data.
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.title: 3. WHAT A SIMULATION IS NOT
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.content: A simulation is a decision-support tool. It describes what happens to a model under the scenarios studied. It does not tell you whether your business will succeed or fail, and no figure it produces should be read as a forecast of your actual revenue, profitability or funding.
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.warning.title: A viability index is not a promise
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.warning.conten: The index measures how robust a model is across the scenarios that were run, on the figures that were available. It is not a probability of success, not a valuation, and not a guarantee of any outcome. Decisions you take on the strength of a run — investing, hiring, borrowing, launching or abandoning — remain entirely yours.
translations.simTerms.no_advice.title: 4. NOT PROFESSIONAL ADVICE
translations.simTerms.no_advice.content: Nothing produced by IDEM Simulation — index, scenarios, factors, risks, recommendations, report — constitutes financial, investment, accounting, tax, legal or regulatory advice. IDEM is not a financial adviser, an auditor, an accountant or a law firm, and no client relationship of that kind arises from your use of the service. Before acting on a run, and in particular before presenting one to a bank, an investor or an administration, have it reviewed by a qualified professional in your jurisdiction.
translations.simTerms.your_document.title: 5. YOUR BUSINESS PLAN
translations.simTerms.your_document.content: You may import a business plan in PDF, Word (.docx) or Markdown. Here is what happens to it, stated plainly so that you know what you are agreeing to:
translations.simTerms.your_document.extraction: The text is extracted from your file. The file itself is not kept after the reading; a scanned document that yields no text is refused.
translations.simTerms.your_document.screening: The text is screened without any AI call. A document that has nothing of a business plan is refused at that point, and nothing of it is sent anywhere.
translations.simTerms.your_document.condensation: Only an extract of the informative passages — on the order of fourteen thousand characters — is sent to the models. Your document is not transmitted in full.
translations.simTerms.your_document.cache: The reading produced from that extract is cached for up to seven days, keyed on a fingerprint of the document, so that re-importing the same file costs nothing. It is attached to your account and to no one else's.
translations.simTerms.your_document.retention: What is kept afterwards is the reading — the profile, the figures, the knowledge items — inside the project it created, under your account, for as long as you keep that project.
translations.simTerms.ai_processing.title: 6. PROCESSING BY AI MODELS
translations.simTerms.ai_processing.content: Running a simulation sends an extract of your project or of your business plan to third-party artificial intelligence providers acting as processors for IDEM. The categories of provider and the safeguards that apply are described in the Privacy Policy, which you also accept before each run. If your plan contains information you are not willing to have processed in that way — personal data of third parties, trade secrets belonging to someone else, information covered by a confidentiality undertaking — remove it before importing.
translations.simTerms.project_creation.title: 7. THE PROJECT CREATED FROM YOUR PLAN
translations.simTerms.project_creation.content: An imported business plan belongs to no existing project, so launching a run creates one in IDEM on your behalf, populated from what the reading yielded: name, description, sector, targets, constraints, budget, and the contact and team details written in your document. That project is yours. It appears in your workspace like any other, it can be edited, and deleting it removes what the reading had stored.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.title: 8. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.content: By launching a run you confirm that:
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.rights: You hold the rights to the document you import, or the authorisation to submit it for processing.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.third_par: You have removed, or are entitled to submit, any personal data of third parties it contains.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.accuracy: The figures you supply, including the answers you give to fill the gaps the engine reports, are yours. A run built on wrong inputs produces a wrong result, and the engine cannot detect that.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.presentat: If you pass a result on to a third party, you keep with it the confidence level and the uncertainties attached to it.
translations.simTerms.billing.title: 9. PRICE AND BILLING
translations.simTerms.billing.content: Simulation is billed separately from the rest of IDEM, because a run spends external research, several agents and computation. The price of the level you choose is shown and confirmed before anything starts, and nothing is charged before that confirmation. During the beta, runs are free: prices are displayed struck through and will apply once the beta ends.
translations.simTerms.availability.title: 10. AVAILABILITY AND FAILED RUNS
translations.simTerms.availability.content: A run takes several minutes and continues if you close the page. The service depends on third-party AI providers and may be slowed or interrupted by them. No amount is retained for a run that does not complete: a failed run is reported as such and can be relaunched. IDEM gives no undertaking as to the duration of a run, nor as to permanent availability of the service.
translations.simTerms.ownership.title: 11. OWNERSHIP OF THE RESULTS
translations.simTerms.ownership.content: You keep every right you hold over the business plan you import and over your project. The results of a run — index, scenarios, factors, report — are yours to use, including commercially, subject to the reservations in section 3 and 4. IDEM keeps its rights over the engine, the prompts, the templates and the methodology that produced them. IDEM may use anonymised, aggregated statistics about runs to improve the service, in the conditions set out in the Privacy Policy.
translations.simTerms.liability.title: 12. LIABILITY
translations.simTerms.liability.content: IDEM Simulation is supplied as is. To the fullest extent permitted by the applicable law, IDEM is not liable for any loss arising from a decision taken on the strength of a run, from an inaccuracy in a result, from an estimate that turned out to be wrong, or from the unavailability of the service. Where liability cannot be excluded, it is limited to the amount you actually paid for the run concerned — which, during the beta, is zero. Nothing in this section limits a liability that cannot be limited by law.
translations.simTerms.liability.warning.title: Read before acting on a result
translations.simTerms.liability.warning.content: A simulation exists to sharpen a decision, never to take it. Do not commit money, staff or a debt on the strength of a run alone, and do not present one as an audited financial projection.
translations.simTerms.changes.title: 13. CHANGES TO THESE TERMS
translations.simTerms.changes.content: These terms may change as the engine changes. Since acceptance is asked before each run, you always accept the version in force at that moment, and the version you accepted is recorded with the run it authorised. Substantial changes are signalled on this page through its effective date.
translations.simTerms.contact.title: 14. CONTACT
translations.simTerms.contact.content: For any question about these terms, about a run, or to ask for the deletion of a project created from an imported business plan, write to contact@idem.africa.

translations.simulation.faq.q1.question: Does IDEM Simulator predict whether my business will succeed?
translations.simulation.faq.q1.answer: No. The results are estimates based on the data, assumptions and scenarios available at the time of analysis. A high index guarantees neither viability nor profitability, and a low index does not mean the project is impossible.
translations.simulation.faq.q2.question: Do I need to have built my project in IDEM to run a simulation?
translations.simulation.faq.q2.answer: No. You can import an existing business plan as PDF, DOCX or plain text: IDEM extracts the activity, market, business model, prices and costs. Projects already built in IDEM get a reduced price, because the deliverables are already available.
translations.simulation.faq.q3.question: What does the simulated viability index measure?
translations.simulation.faq.q3.answer: It measures how robust the model is across the scenarios that were run: how well it keeps holding as the factors deteriorate. It is always shown together with a confidence level and the list of main uncertainties.
translations.simulation.faq.q4.question: Is simulation included in IDEM?
translations.simulation.faq.q4.answer: No, it is billed separately because it spends external research, several agents and compute. The amount is shown and confirmed before the run starts. The full report can be bought with the simulation or later.
